doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Conducting for Basie and being vetoed as his successor
summary: Terry sometimes led the band; Norman Granz blocked his taking over after Basie died.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: When Basie passed – let me ask you, before I ask you that – did you – I think I read somewhere that oftentimes Basie would have you conduct the band or . . .

He would have a lot of us from time to time do – kick the band off and stop it or something like that, but if he was going to be off the stand or something, socializing heavily or something, we – either one of us would take the responsibility of doing that, but for the most part, he would get a saxophone player, because he was down front, and all he had to do was stand up and say, “bing.”
When the – when Basie passed, did you want to run that band? Or was it not . . .

At one point I was asked to front the band, and I was up for consideration. This was before Thad [Jones] or Joe Williams or any of the cats that took over. Was it Frank Foster or whatever. Before any of them were considered, they asked me. Norman Granz was on the board, and Norman vetoed. He said, “No. I will not allow him to do that.” I said – somebody called him Smedley – I said, “Smedley, why did you not want me?” He said, “Because you’d be dead in a year’s time.” So I suppose I have to thank Smedley for not allowing me to front the band.”
